title: Your first map
summary: Create a map, add a source and put interactive places on it.
learn: A source owns the data. A layer decides how to draw it. Start with three places, then fit the view or select a place to inspect its details.
hint: Click a place · drag to pan · scroll to zoom
note: Real city coordinates, without a basemap. No external tile requests.

title: Points that change
summary: Style by properties, edit one point and hide it without deleting it.
learn: Expressions read feature properties and interaction state. Change a feature's status, move it, or apply a layer-specific visibility override while keeping its identity.
hint: Drag a point · click to select · try the data controls
note: Synthetic station data in planar coordinates. Changes are made through the public API.

title: Lines, fills & holes
summary: Draw a route and a polygon with a real opening in its center.
learn: Line strings and polygon rings are separate geometry types. The first polygon ring is the outside boundary; the next ring is a hole. Switch the fill or route independently.
hint: Toggle a layer · zoom into the polygon opening
note: Synthetic route and site plan. The polygon hole is geometry, not a background-colored overlay.

title: Connected data
summary: Move an endpoint and let its connected line follow in the same update.
learn: Stable feature references identify the endpoints. A lineBetween binding derives the route from their positions. The relation records their connection without duplicating geometry.
hint: Drag an endpoint · use Move endpoint for a keyboard-accessible update
note: Two synthetic stations and one derived line. No animation loop or manual line repair.

title: Bring your GeoJSON
summary: Edit a small FeatureCollection, import it and export the stored data.
learn: GeoJSON uses [longitude, latitude], not [latitude, longitude]. Importing replaces this example's source atomically; a rejected import leaves the previously accepted data on the map.
hint: Edit the GeoJSON · import · export to inspect the result
note: Input stays in your browser. This example accepts at most 64 KiB and 100 point features.

title: Labels & image pins
summary: Reuse one SVG pin and label places from their feature properties.
learn: Register an image once, reference it from a point layer, then add a label layer over the same source. Toggle labels and move pins without creating one DOM element per symbol.
hint: Drag a pin · toggle the labels · change their text
note: The SVG image is embedded in the source. Labels use system fonts; no asset download is needed.

title: Raster tiles
summary: Add an XYZ tile source and switch between demo tiles and OpenStreetMap.
learn: A raster source requests tiles for the visible view. The default grid is an inline SVG tile; live OpenStreetMap is requested only after you choose it. Attribution follows the active source.
hint: Choose a basemap · pan and zoom · check its attribution
note: OpenStreetMap needs an internet connection and follows its tile usage policy. No prefetching or offline caching.

title: A plugin is a function
summary: Install a small pin plugin, use its API and remove all its resources.
learn: map.use() passes a context into a plain function. Return your own API and register cleanup in ownership order. Removing the plugin removes its layer, source and HTML badge.
hint: Install the plugin · add a pin · remove it and watch its resources disappear
note: A focused version of the existing plugin playground. No external assets or runtime dependencies.
